status: pre-registered before any v4 candidate was scored on any dev file at the ledger level; the engine step (GES under each score) was smoke-run on 6 dev files per family only to time it and to check the plumbing (gauss re-implementation equals ges 1.1.0 GaussObsL0Pen's CPDAG on the first file)
why: X1-X4 (analysis/reports/q2_explain_dev.md, sheet A) and the family-2 read (analysis/results/q2_v3/family2_read.json) point to one lever: the engines score with a linear-Gaussian model while the mechanisms are nonlinear or discrete. Family 2: precision at half coverage 0.851 on its linear track against 0.742 on its nonlinear track. X5: a pretrained engine (AVICI) does not help. So the candidate change is the score inside GES.
question: Does a GES score that fits nonlinear additive and discrete mechanisms raise the ledger's DV-1 precision at half coverage on CausalArena dev, semantic family, without losing the formula family or calibration?

data.dev: CausalArena dev split (plans/splits.json), regime D (one file, 1,000 rows), 125 files per family, semantic and formula
data.held_out: family 2 replicate 1 (v4/heldout_gen.py: 500 files, same 50 source scenarios and graphs G_D as replicate 0, new draws), generated on sheet B and sealed: no kernel may score it before plans/v4_freeze.json exists. Read once, by the winner only. CausalArena's test split is not read again (read by v2 and v3).

knobs.G0: v3's GES (ges.fit_bic: forward, backward, turning) from the v3 engine cache: baseline
knobs.G1: gauss score, forward + backward (no turning): search control, never adoptable
knobs.A1: additive score (hinge basis z, (z-q25)+, (z-q50)+, (z-q75)+ per continuous parent; indicators for parents with <= 10 levels), lam 1, forward + backward
knobs.R1: rff score (linear terms + min(80, 20|pa|) random Fourier features, Gaussian kernel bandwidth sqrt(|pa|), ridge alpha 1, df = trace of the hat matrix), lam 1, forward + backward

fixed: PC (with its recorded tests), jitter, rule C3, the v3 direction view (meek_r1 and meek_r3 not acted on), DV-1 claims, claim features and the confidence recipe (gradient boosting + isotonic map) are v3's. The confidence model is refitted per knob out of fold by scenario (5 folds), as kernel/v3.py evaluate --split dev. GES timeout 900 s per file: a timeout is a typed failure and that file's ledger is PC-only for that knob (counted).

metrics.landmark: precision at half coverage, coverage, ECE, with scenario-cluster bootstrap intervals (B = 2000, seed 20261014), kernel/v3.scored
metrics.paired: precision_half(knob) - precision_half(G0) on the same resampled scenarios (v4/dev.paired_half)
metrics.engine: GES output alone: directed F1 (undecided pairs oriented at random, per-file seed), skeleton F1, false and missed adjacencies per file; share of files where the knob's score of the true DAG is at least the score GES reports for its output

predictions.Q1: semantic: the better additive knob (A1 or A2) raises GES skeleton F1 over G1 by at least 0.03 (paired mean)
predictions.Q2: semantic: under A1 the true DAG scores at least as high as GES's output on at least 0.30 of files (G0: 0.025, X1)
predictions.Q3: semantic: A1 reduces GES false adjacencies per file by at least 20 % against G1
predictions.Q4: dropping the turning phase alone is neutral: |precision_half(G1) - precision_half(G0)| <= 0.01, semantic
predictions.Q5: formula: the best eligible knob's precision_half is not below G0's by more than 0.01

rule.eligible: semantic coverage_half >= 0.5, semantic ECE <= 0.05, formula precision_half >= G0's - 0.01
rule.adoptable: eligible, and the paired semantic gain over G0 has point >= 0.02 and lower end > 0
rule.winner: the adoptable knob with the highest semantic precision_half; none adoptable -> v3 stays the kernel
rule.then_adopt: freeze v4 (plans/v4_freeze.json: the v3 trees plus v4/, the knob, the confidence models refitted on all dev files) and read it once on the held-out family; ER-2 / ER-3 reported for family 2 beside v3's replicate-0 read, never pooled
rule.then_none: the score lever alone is not enough: wave C records it (TGT-18, BLD-18) and turns to the next lever in the lever map; no held-out file is read

failure_modes_named_in_advance: non-score-equivalent scores inside a CPDAG search: the turning phase is dropped for every new knob and G1 measures the effect of dropping it
overfitting from basis columns: penalty counts every basis column; A2 doubles it
discrete children are modelled as Gaussian residuals (the X3 floor stays a floor)
the ledger's engine label still reads 'ges.fit_bic' for the knobs: provenance text only, claims unaffected; a v4 freeze must relabel
GES's reported score drifts from a fresh rescoring by up to about 0.03 (X1): Q2 uses the package's final score, so ties within 0.1 count as 'at least'
CPU family: hashes differ across hosts, claim structure does not (wave canary); dev numbers are computed on Uzair's machine
compute: engine step 15-30 s per file per knob (sandbox smoke on 12 files: G1 16, A1 18, A2 15, R1 29 s mean; no failures): 4 knobs x 250 files, about 5.4 core-hours; evaluate about 20-30 min
